tickets.title: Explicit finite lower bound max(fan-in lg n, counting lg n!/floor(n/2), Kahale Fibonacci) in Lean
tickets.first_deliverable: Lean: Sorts net -> n.factorial <= 2^(comparator count) via ComparisonTrace.exec_trace_injective; then D(n)*floor(n/2) >= lg n! and D(n) >= clog 2 n; one combined finite theorem
tickets.notes: Done on lb-01-finite: SortingDepth.minimum_ge_max_bounds (every n): max(clog 2 n, countingBound n, kahaleBound n) <= D(n), countingBound n = ceil(clog 2 n! / floor(n/2)), kahaleBound = least d with n fib(d+1) <= 2^(d+1)(d+1)^2. Counting proved self-contained (comparator at most 2-to-1 on inputs; layer <= floor(n/2) comparators), not via ComparisonTrace. Corollary D(2^k) >= 2k-2 (k >= 2), D(2^16) >= 30. Axiom-clean. Constant unchanged.

tickets.title: Two-sided (zero and one) certificate-height relaxation: does joint (h0,h1) with the intersection / n+2 coupling exceed 3.2706?
tickets.first_deliverable: none (barrier): joint (z,o) relaxation with Z, O, graded G, n+2 coupling and active width W has rate exactly 3.2706
tickets.notes: Histogram form: the z-projection is Kahale's system (n <= U_d, kernel-checked), and equal-z pairing passes both sides at N_d for d <= 1024, so the rate is exactly 3.2706. Positional form: the block-halving schedule, with over-wide blocks idled, meets Z, O, G (both sides) and W at N_d for every tested d <= 1024 (exact run-length check). Per-wire two-sided data is exactly the rank interval (min zero size lo+1, min one size n-hi). The zero and one requirements bind on disjoint wire sets, so the n+2 coupling never binds. An all-d proof of the one side is numerical only (the schedule is not exactly self-dual). Next: cross-wire disjointness D_ij (LB-24).

tickets.title: Coupled information/certificate tradeoff: Kahale-extremal schedules waste comparison information
tickets.first_deliverable: Exact or analytic sum of (1-h_g) on the positional barrier family and sorted-block families as a function of d; if the slot saving rho is well above 0.388 on extremal schedules, state the tradeoff inequality
tickets.notes: Counting (2) and Kahale (3.27) are each tight on their own relaxations; a joint inequality could beat both. Risk: the charging problem of LB-26 returns.

tickets.title: Depth lower bound for epsilon-halvers and approximate selectors from the Kahale machinery

tickets.notes: Calibrates upper-side halver/separator ideas (UB-04, UB-06). May only reproduce a lg(1/eps)-type bound.

tickets.title: Kernel-checked exact D(n) for small n (n <= 8, stretch 10)
tickets.first_deliverable: D(4)=3 and D(5)=5 by kernel decide over normalized first layers (no native_decide); measure kernel cost before scaling
tickets.notes: Target is a published result, not yet formalized here. D(n) is known exactly for n <= 17 (Parberry; Bundala-Zavodny; Codish et al.); D(18..32) >= 10 only. No asymptotic consequence.
